claim_text: DWP says it identified a cyber incident affecting its systems
summary: The Department for Work and Pensions says it identified "a cyber incident affecting our systems" and took some of its online services offline as a precaution. It announced this on GOV.UK on the morning of Nov 27.
detail: DWP has not said when it found the incident, what kind of incident it is or how it happened.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: GOV.UK notice: "We have taken some DWP online services offline as a precaution after we identified a cyber incident affecting our systems"; the BBC and The Register quote the same statement.

claim_text: Some DWP online services are offline
summary: Some DWP online services are offline and may be temporarily unavailable. DWP says it is working to bring them back as quickly as possible and that people who need help should call their usual benefit line. It has given no return time.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: GOV.UK notice (updated 14:45 GMT): "Some DWP online services may be temporarily unavailable" and "If customers need help, they should call their usual benefit line"; BBC: it "was not clear when" services would be back.
notes: The notice first told people to try again later; the 14:45 GMT update replaced that with the advice to call their usual benefit line.

claim_text: DWP says regular benefit and pension payments are not affected
summary: DWP says regular benefit and pension payments are not affected and will be paid as normal.
detail: This is DWP's own statement; nobody outside it has said so yet. On Nov 27 some Universal Credit claimants told the BBC they had not received their payments; asked about this, DWP repeated that regular payments are not affected and said anyone having problems with a payment should call its benefit phoneline (BBC, 14:44 GMT).
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: GOV.UK notice: "Regular benefit and pension payments are not affected and will be paid as normal." BBC live page, 14:44 GMT: DWP "reiterated that regular payments have not been affected".

claim_text: DWP is working with the National Cyber Security Centre
summary: DWP says it is working closely with the National Cyber Security Centre and the Government Cyber Coordination Centre to investigate and to bring services back online.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: GOV.UK notice: "We are working closely with the National Cyber Security Centre and Government Cyber Coordination Centre to investigate".

claim_text: Online services for pensions, Universal Credit, PIP and Tell Us Once could not be used
summary: The BBC says that around 12:00 GMT on Nov 27 the online systems for pensions, Universal Credit and PIP applications, and Tell Us Once, still could not be accessed, and that State Pension application services are down.
detail: DWP itself has not said which services are offline. The BBC first reported the same services unavailable around 9 AM GMT; City AM reports Universal Credit sign-in problems.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: BBC: "As of around 12:00 GMT on Friday, the online systems for pensions, universal credit and Pip applications ... could not be accessed"; live page: "Services that allow people to apply for their state pension are also down".

claim_text: DWP has not said what kind of incident it was or whether personal data was accessed
summary: DWP has not said what type of cyber incident it is dealing with, or whether any personal data has been accessed.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: BBC: it "has not confirmed what type of cyber incident is impacting its systems or whether personal data has been accessed"; The Register: officials have not said whether any data is thought compromised.

claim_text: DWP says it will never ask for personal information by text or email
summary: DWP reminds people that it will never ask for their personal information by text or email, and links to GOV.UK guidance on avoiding and reporting scams and phishing.
detail: On Nov 27 DWP also warned people, in a post on social media quoted by the BBC, to "be on guard for unsolicited calls or texts".
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: GOV.UK notice (updated 14:45 GMT): "As always, we will never ask for your personal information via text or email." BBC live page, 12:48 GMT: DWP warns people to "be on guard for unsolicited calls or texts".
notes: Until its 14:45 GMT update the GOV.UK notice said: "As always, we will never message you to ask for bank details or ask you to click on links." DWP changed the wording; the claim follows the page as it stands.

claim_text: The Legal Aid Agency took services offline after a breach in 2025
summary: In April 2025 the government said attackers had got into the Legal Aid Agency's online services and taken a significant amount of personal data; the agency took some services offline. No source links it to this incident.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: BBC: "In April 2025, the government reported that cyber attackers had breached the Legal Aid Agency's online services" and "The agency took some services offline".

claim_text: DWP is the UK's biggest public service department
summary: The Department for Work and Pensions runs the UK's welfare, pensions and child maintenance policy. It pays the State Pension and working-age, disability and ill-health benefits to around 20 million claimants and customers.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: GOV.UK: DWP "is responsible for welfare, pensions and child maintenance policy" and "administers the State Pension and a range of working age, disability and ill health benefits to around 20 million claimants and customers".

claim_text: Downing Street says there is no evidence other departments are being targeted
summary: The BBC reports that Downing Street said there was no evidence that a "malicious actor" is targeting other government departments. The nature of the DWP incident has not been confirmed.
detail: We have not found this statement on a government page; it is as the BBC reports it.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: BBC: "While the nature of the DWP incident has not yet been confirmed, Downing Street said there was no evidence that a 'malicious actor' is targeting other government departments."

claim_text: It is not yet known whether a hack or a technical failure caused it
summary: The BBC says it is not clear whether DWP was hit by a hack or a technical failure, and that there is no evidence at this stage of a breach at DWP by hackers. DWP has not said what kind of incident it was.
detail: Problem reports about gov.uk on Downdetector rose from about 7:20 PM GMT on Nov 26, the BBC says, but it is not clear whether they are related.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: BBC: "it was not clear whether the DWP had been impacted by a hack or a technical failure"; BBC live page: "there is no evidence at this stage of a breach at the DWP by hackers".
notes: Both are BBC reporting; they count as one source.

claim_text: Discussion threads suggest old systems, a supplier or human error rather than a sophisticated attack
summary: On Hacker News, several commenters expect an ordinary cause, such as old IT systems, a supplier's compromise or a human mistake, and others link it to rumours of a cryptography breakthrough. The thread raises questions; it is not evidence.
detail: No commenter offers evidence. DWP has not said what the incident was.
label: Rumor
why_it_supports: The thread shows the questions readers are raising; it is an anonymous discussion and is not evidence for any cause.

claim_text: Downing Street says the incident was detected on Nov 26 and an investigation is looking at who is behind it
summary: The BBC reports that the prime minister's official spokesperson called it a "live and ongoing incident" detected on Nov 26, and said an investigation is looking at who is behind it. Officials could not rule out a malicious actor.
detail: Asked whether a malicious actor could be behind it, the spokesperson said "we are looking at what it could be", the BBC reports. This is not a statement that anyone got in.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: BBC live page, 12:16 GMT: "An investigation is under way to establish who is behind the cyber incident"; officials "could not rule out that a malicious actor was behind" it; it "was detected yesterday".
notes: We have not found the briefing on a government page; it is as the BBC reports it.

claim_text: Downing Street says there is currently no evidence of customer data loss
summary: The BBC reports that the prime minister's official spokesperson said "currently there is no evidence of customer data loss", adding that the investigation is ongoing. DWP itself has not said whether personal data was accessed.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: BBC live page, 12:16 GMT, quoting the spokesperson: "Currently there is no evidence of customer data loss ... But the investigation is ongoing so I'm not going to get ahead of that process." The BBC report says the same.
notes: Both are BBC reporting; they count as one source.

claim_text: Some Universal Credit claimants say their payments have not arrived
summary: The BBC says some people who receive Universal Credit told it on Nov 27 that their payments, including an advance, had not arrived, and one that a pension payment had not. DWP says regular payments are not affected.
detail: These are individual accounts given to the BBC. Asked about them, DWP repeated that regular payments are not affected and said anyone with a payment problem should call its benefit phoneline. Nobody has said how many people are affected or whether the cyber incident caused the delays.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: BBC live page, 12:56 GMT: some claimants "have not yet received their payments"; 14:44 GMT: "We contacted the DWP about this. In response, they reiterated that regular payments have not been affected."

claim_text: The Work and Pensions Secretary calls it a "serious cyber incident" and says there is no evidence anyone's data has been compromised
summary: The BBC says the Work and Pensions Secretary called the outage a "serious cyber incident". He said services were taken down to protect personal data, there is no evidence anyone's data was compromised, and payments will be made as usual.
detail: He said the department is working with the National Cyber Security Centre to get systems running again and that investigations into the cause are ongoing. No evidence of data being compromised is not the same as a finding that none was taken; DWP and the Information Commissioner's Office have not said.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: BBC live page, 13:44 GMT: he "describes today's outage as a 'serious cyber incident'"; "there's no evidence that anyone's data has been compromised"; "investigations into the cause are ongoing".
notes: As the BBC reports his update; we have not found a transcript on a government page.

claim_text: DWP says nobody will be sanctioned if the cyber incident stopped them attending or updating their claim
summary: DWP told the BBC that while it works to resolve the incident, customers who cannot attend appointments or update their circumstances will not be sanctioned. Sanctions already processed earlier still apply.
detail: Universal Credit claimants who cannot reach the online service had told the BBC they feared losing payments for not updating their journal. This is DWP's word as the BBC reports it; we have not found it on a DWP page.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: BBC live page, 14:58 GMT, quoting a DWP spokeswoman: "customers who do not attend or cannot update their circumstances will not be sanctioned. Sanctions already processed earlier will still apply".
